extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians preparing submissions to the Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society (authors of expository mathematical articles, book review authors by invitation)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting manuscripts (primarily expository research articles) to the Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society, including required metadata, submission routes, post-acceptance steps, and rights/permissions rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article type and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulletin publishes expository articles on contemporary mathematical research, written in a way that gives insight to mathematicians who may not be experts in the particular topic. The Bulletin also publishes reviews of selected books in mathematics and short articles in the Mathematical Perspectives section, both by invitation only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit expository material aimed at a broad mathematical readership rather than highly specialized technical reports; book reviews and Mathematical Perspectives content are typically by invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract is required. It should be a brief technical description of the new material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts are made available electronically worldwide; no abstracts appear in the printed journal starting in 1998.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method — Centralized Manuscript Processing
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS uses Centralized Manuscript Processing for initial submissions. The preferred method of submission is to upload a PDF file using the Initial Manuscript Submission form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an alternative one copy may be mailed to the Centralized Manuscript Processing address, but the electronic Initial Manuscript Submission form is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission metadata when mailing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper copy is forwarded to the AMS, the following information is required with the submission: Name of the journal to which the paper is submitted; Name of the corresponding author; Contact information including email address and mailing address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All contact information, particularly email addresses, must be supplied to avoid delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest an appropriate Editor
rubrics_metrics.description: The author should suggest an appropriate Editor to review the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are asked to indicate which Editor would be suitable for reviewing their manuscript (helps the editorial assignment process).

rubrics_metrics.name: No simultaneous submissions / prior publication prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No paper that has been previously published, or is being considered for publication elsewhere, should be submitted to the American Mathematical Society, nor may a paper that is under consideration by the American Mathematical Society be submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit the same manuscript to multiple journals or submit work that has already appeared in print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Included with the footnotes to the paper should be the 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification representing the primary and secondary subjects of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the appropriate primary and secondary MSC codes in the paper's footnotes so the AMS can classify the article correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AMS author resources and style files
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to use AMS-prepared style files in preparing their papers. The AMS Author Resource Center provides TeX Resources, the AMS Style Guide, the Mathematics Subject Classification, and further useful tools for preparing your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided TeX templates/Overleaf templates and follow AMS style guidance to reduce formatting issues and speed production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing graphics and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should consult the Joint Author Guidelines for Preparing Accessible Mathematics Content when preparing graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AMS guidance to make figures and graphics accessible (e.g., readable labels, appropriate formats) and compatible with AMS production workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions, copying, and reuse policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual readers and nonprofit libraries acting for them are permitted to make fair use of the material (e.g., copy an article for teaching or research). Republication, systematic copying, or multiple reproduction of any material is permitted only under license from the American Mathematical Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for permission to reuse portions of AMS publication content are handled by the Copyright Clearance Center; if the author holds copyright for particular material, requests should be addressed directly to the author(s). Copyright ownership is indicated in the notice on the first page of each article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance: Consent to Publish and copyright agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a paper has been accepted for publication, authors should follow the online Submission Instructions. All authors must submit the Consent to Publish. All authors must agree regarding the Copyright Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete required author forms promptly after acceptance; follow the online instructions for providing signed consent and copyright arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Access selection and license
rubrics_metrics.description: If the article is to be published in one of the AMS Open Access journals, authors must agree which Creative Commons License will be selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors publishing open access need to select the appropriate CC license and agree among coauthors which license to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprints / author access to published article
rubrics_metrics.description: Offprints are provided free of charge in electronic form to all authors. A downloadable and printable PDF version of each article is available from the AMS website following print publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors receive notification email with access information as soon as an issue is published in print; this provides permanent electronic access to the published material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for inquiries about accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Any inquiries concerning a paper that has been accepted for publication that cannot be answered via the manuscript tracking system should be sent to the Electronic PrePress Department, American Mathematical Society (address provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the manuscript tracking system first; for unresolved issues, contact the Electronic PrePress Department by email or postal mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and archiving expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal is indexed in Mathematical Reviews®, Science Citation Index®, and other indexes, and is archived in Portico and CLOCKSS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware that published articles will be discoverable via standard indexing services and preserved in long-term archiving systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to article PDFs may require subscription
rubrics_metrics.description: A current active subscription to the electronic version of this journal is required to view article PDFs in all volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While abstracts, references, and bibliographic information are freely viewable, full PDF access may be limited to subscribers or AMS members; authors receive electronic offprints regardless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools and services recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS points authors to language editing services (Charlesworth Author Services), AMS journal article templates on Overleaf, and other useful tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may use recommended services and templates to improve manuscript clarity and formatting prior to submission.
